metadata.title: Odin OS (Phase B.2): Adversarial Assurance, Evidence Integrity & Hardware-Enforced PMP Wordline Gating for Sovereign AI Agents
metadata.description:
Odin OS (Phase B.2: Adversarial Assurance & Evidence Integrity) is a bare-metal, zero-allocation (#![no_std]) 64-bit RISC-V microkernel that anchors autonomous AI agent capability boundaries directly into physical silicon memory protection hardware. Operating on the central axiom that state that cannot prove its right to exist cannot be committed, Odin OS enforces capability containment via cache-line aligned 256-byte binary tokens termed TransitionDeeds.

Phase B.2 establishes genuine zero-allocation Ed25519 asymmetric cryptographic authority verification against a pinned root public key, bi-directional W^X hardware memory enforcement, temporal capability lease revocation, a deterministic 17-case adversarial verification matrix, and 100% mutation testing sensitivity. The publication includes machine-verifiable JSON receipts and empirical proof executing against local neural inference on google/gemma-4-e4b: authorized mutations commit in a single clock cycle, while adversarial prompt injection jailbreaks trigger hardware Store Access Faults (mcause = 0x07), leaving zero bits flipped in physical memory.
